links.outcome: Contour accuracy for manual vs AI-only vs physician-plus-AI delineation
links.effect: Mean vDSC 0.857 manual, 0.896 AI, 0.902 AI-assisted; HD95 8.01, 5.62, 5.20 mm; sequential significant improvement (p<0.0001); time median 10.0 vs 55.0 min.
links.quote: These data show a sequential and significant improvement in accuracy from manual, to AI, and to AI-assisted delineation ( p < 0.0001), a trend that was further supported by sDSC ( p < 0.0001) (Supplementary Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: Accuracy of physician-revised AI contours vs unrevised AI contours
links.effect: AI-assisted (physician-revised) contours significantly more accurate than AI-only for 6 of 11 OARs (54.5%); revision eliminated EC-related trachea accuracy drop.
links.quote: AI-assisted delineation also achieved significantly higher accuracy than AI delineation for 6 out of 11 OARs (54.5%): the heart, aorta, liver, trachea, spinal cord, and esophagus (Fig. 2a, b and Supplementary Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: Performance by center for AI-assisted vs manual delineation
links.effect: Performance hierarchy held across all five centers (p<0.0001), but AI-assisted showed no advantage for trachea in Center 4 and aorta in Center 5.
links.quote: However, AI-assisted delineation failed to show an advantage over the manual method in a few specific instances: for the trachea both in Center 4 and in patients with EC, and for the aorta in Center 5 (Supplementary Figs. 4 – 6 ).

links.outcome: Change in manual contouring accuracy over time among less-experienced physicians using AI
links.effect: Of 25 less-experienced physicians, 19 (76%) no change, 3 (12%) improved, 3 (12%) declined in manual vDSC.
links.quote: In contrast, three (12%) experienced a decline in M-vDSC ( p = 0.042, 0.029, and 0.013), characterized by under- or over-segmentation of clear anatomical boundaries and increased OAR overlap (Supplementary Fig. 21 ).

links.outcome: Segmentation accuracy compared with alternative models on the same cohort
links.effect: iCurveE: vDSC 0.896, HD95 5.62 mm; nnU-Net: 0.850, 12.05 mm; TotalSegmentator: 0.781, 19.07 mm; both comparisons p < 0.0001.
links.quote: The iCurveE model achieved a significantly superior performance, with a mean volumetric Dice similarity coefficient (vDSC) of 0.896 and a 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 5.62 mm, compared to both the nnU-Net (vDSC, 0.850; HD95, 12.05 mm; p < 0.0001) and TotalSegmentator (vDSC, 0.781; HD95, 19.07 mm; p < 0.0001) models.

links.outcome: Contour accuracy after physician review and modification versus unmodified AI outputs
links.effect: Physician revision significantly improved accuracy for 6 out of 11 OARs (54.5%); mean vDSC increased from 0.896 to 0.902, and mean HD95 decreased from 5.62 mm to 5.20 mm.
links.quote: AI-assisted delineation also achieved significantly higher accuracy than AI delineation for 6 out of 11 OARs (54.5%): the heart, aorta, liver, trachea, spinal cord, and esophagus (Fig. 2a, b and Supplementary Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: AI segmentation accuracy differences between lung cancer and non-lung-cancer patients
links.effect: AI accuracy was significantly lower for the heart, trachea, and esophagus in lung cancer patients; no consistent multi-metric differences occurred for lungs or bronchial tree. Numerical effect sizes were not reported.
links.quote: In patients with LC, the model’s segmentation accuracy (i.e., AI-vDSC, HD95, and sDSC) for the heart, trachea, and esophagus was significantly lower than in non-LC patients; however, no consistent multi-metric differences were observed for the lungs and bronchial tree (Supplementary Fig. 8 ).

links.outcome: Changes in less-experienced physicians’ manual contouring accuracy during AI use
links.effect: Among 25 physicians, 19 (76%) showed no significant change, three (12%) improved, and three (12%) declined; decline p = 0.042, 0.029, and 0.013. Causation by AI reliance was not established.
links.quote: In contrast, three (12%) experienced a decline in M-vDSC ( p = 0.042, 0.029, and 0.013), characterized by under- or over-segmentation of clear anatomical boundaries and increased OAR overlap (Supplementary Fig. 21 ).

links.outcome: Accuracy of manual, AI standalone, and AI-assisted delineation
links.effect: Accuracy sequentially improved from manual (mean vDSC 0.857) to AI standalone (0.896) to AI-assisted delineation (0.902).
links.quote: These data show a sequential and significant improvement in accuracy from manual, to AI, and to AI-assisted delineation ( p < 0.0001), a trend that was further supported by sDSC ( p < 0.0001) (Supplementary Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: Comparative accuracy against alternative models
links.effect: The iCurveE model (mean vDSC 0.896) significantly outperformed competing models nnU-Net (0.850) and TotalSegmentator (0.781).
links.quote: The iCurveE model achieved a significantly superior performance, with a mean volumetric Dice similarity coefficient (vDSC) of 0.896 and a 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 5.62 mm, compared to both the nnU-Net (vDSC, 0.850; HD95, 12.05 mm; p < 0.0001) and TotalSegmentator (vDSC, 0.781; HD95, 19.07 mm; p < 0.0001) models.

links.outcome: Model accuracy by CT slice thickness
links.effect: CT scans with a 5 mm slice thickness resulted in lower model accuracy for humeral heads compared to thinner slices.
links.quote: Furthermore, compared to thinner slices (<5 mm), scans with a 5 mm slice thickness demonstrated lower model accuracy only for the left and right humeral heads (Supplementary Fig. 11 ).

links.outcome: Segmentation accuracy in clinical subgroups
links.effect: Model segmentation accuracy for the heart, trachea, and esophagus was significantly lower in patients with lung cancer than those without.
links.quote: In patients with LC, the model’s segmentation accuracy (i.e., AI-vDSC, HD95, and sDSC) for the heart, trachea, and esophagus was significantly lower than in non-LC patients; however, no consistent multi-metric differences were observed for the lungs and bronchial tree (Supplementary Fig. 8 ).

links.outcome: Change in manual contouring accuracy over time
links.effect: Three of 25 less-experienced physicians (12%) experienced a significant decline in their manual contouring accuracy over time after using AI.
links.quote: In contrast, three (12%) experienced a decline in M-vDSC ( p = 0.042, 0.029, and 0.013), characterized by under- or over-segmentation of clear anatomical boundaries and increased OAR overlap (Supplementary Fig. 21 ).

screen.practice: clinician review/editing of AI-generated contours (AI-assisted vs manual delineation)
screen.reason: Prospective multi-center reader trial evaluating clinician performance and time efficiency when using AI assistance versus manual delineation for radiation therapy planning.

primary.practice: AI-assisted contouring vs manual clinician delineation
